analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB write occurs because ZSTD_execSequenceEnd computes `oend_w = oend - WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH` without guarding small output buffers. When `oend` is smaller than `WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH` (as in this PoV’s tiny 176-byte destination block), `oend_w` underflows before the destination buffer. `ZSTD_safecopy()` then takes the `op <= oend_w` path and performs `ZSTD_wildcopy()` to an invalid bound, followed by leftover byte copies, resulting in a write past the allocated heap buffer. Crash is observed at ZSTD_safecopy line 753, but root cause is unsafe end-pointer arithmetic and bound handling in ZSTD_execSequenceEnd/ZSTD_safecopy for near-end sequences on small dst buffers.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer input is parsed as a Blosc frame and routed to zstd decompression (`blosc_d -> zstd_wrap_decompress -> ZSTD_decompressDCtx -> ... -> ZSTD_decompressSequences`). A crafted compressed sequence makes execution enter the slow path `ZSTD_execSequenceEnd` (near-end match/literal conditions). With a small output block size from the frame metadata, `oend_w` becomes invalid (`oend - WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH` underflow), and sequence copy logic writes beyond the destination allocation, triggering ASan heap-buffer-overflow.
